feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: U.S. imposes sweeping sanctions on International Criminal Court
entry.summary: The U.S. has announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowing to dismantle the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal.

entry.title: Week in Politics: Hegseth's livestream backlash; Greece ambassador Guilfoyle scandal
entry.summary: Bipartisan blowback on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plans to livestream a military execution, plus a scandal involving Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US Ambassador to Greece.

entry.title: On the ground in Ohio's 9th District: The battleground shaping next month's midterms
entry.summary: Ohio is a critical battleground in next month's midterms elections. NPR's Scott Simon traveled to the state's 9th Congressional District to hear from voters about their priorities.

entry.title: After losing ground with Latino voters, Democrats are turning to influencers for help
entry.summary: Democrats are hoping to win back Latino voters who have soured on both parties. They hope Latino content creators will bridge the gap.

entry.title: Trump says U.S. to get diesel from Russia, relaxing pressure on Moscow to ease prices before midterms
entry.summary: Trump says the U.S. will obtain diesel from Russia, relaxing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow, to combat prices before midterms. He said he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.

entry.title: Trump's Affordable Suit
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with New York Times fashion reporter Jacob Gallagher about President Trump's apparent choice to wear a suit from the budget menswear chain Jos. A. Bank.

entry.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
entry.summary: The Trump administration's effort to return Ahmed Soliman to the U.S. come after an Arizona judge said his deportation violated due process.

entry.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
entry.summary: If you're using the U.S. Postal Service to return a ballot close to Election Day, officials recommend getting it postmarked at a post office to avoid getting caught up in mail processing changes.

entry.title: Republican congressman tries to outrun a potential blue wave in New York toss-up seat
entry.summary: Rep. Mike Lawler, R-NY, is in a tight race for re-election in a toss-up district that could help determine control of Congress in November.

entry.title: 25 years later an Afghan couple looks back at the invasion
entry.summary: Twenty-five years ago this week, the U.S. invaded Afghanistan. For StoryCorps, one Afghan couple offers an account of their experience after the invasion and eventual U.S. withdrawal.
